concepts.name: Aperture
concepts.position: A parent identity for research, code and participation.
concepts.idea: Two offset brackets define one open field. The space between them is as deliberate as the ink: a compact metaphor for rules that leave room for participation.
concepts.lettering: Lowercase, medium weight, open counters. Custom upright t forms and square i dot, with Manrope-derived n/c/a outlines and optical spacing.
concepts.benefit: Strongest balance of institutional restraint and Tincta’s geometric art heritage. No standalone letter silhouette.
concepts.risk: Offset brackets are a familiar design vocabulary. Review against software, custody and infrastructure marks; avoid adding a containing square or linking it into a chain.
concepts.refine: Explore asymmetric proportions and opening widths; refine the n–c spacing, t shoulder and a terminal; compare a rounded and a sharper master.

concepts.name: Fold
concepts.position: The strongest direction for a financial technology company.
concepts.idea: A broad horizontal plane and an upright plane meet across a diagonal cut. The fold suggests a published edition becoming a structure.
concepts.lettering: Title case, compact grotesk, moderate weight. Instrument Sans outlines with custom pair spacing, led by the flat capital T.
concepts.benefit: Bold silhouette, very simple reproduction and a clear move toward a corporate identity.
concepts.risk: May read as a 7, flag or folded arrow. Angular finance and exchange logos are crowded; the cut and proportions need further differentiation.
concepts.refine: Test three seam angles and stem positions; resolve the possible 7 reading; develop a distinctive t terminal shared by the lettering and fold.

concepts.name: Ligature
concepts.position: A research publisher with a restrained institutional voice.
concepts.idea: A compact T/C monogram pairs the opening initial with the central consonant. A shared top edge brings the two letters into one editorial signature.
concepts.lettering: Spaced uppercase with a moderate stroke. Instrument Sans outlines with revised T/I, C/T and T/A spacing.
concepts.benefit: The most editorial direction; works naturally on research covers and formal communications.
concepts.risk: TC can imply two words, a consultancy or a fashion house. Less distinctive and less connected to participation than Aperture; monogram complexity is weakest at 16 px.
concepts.refine: Test whether the monogram reads as one signature; simplify the shared junction; tighten uppercase tracking for navigation.
